must_fix.title: HEAD responses get the ETag of an empty body when the handler omits the body for HEAD (e.g. http.ServeContent/FileServer), so it differs from GET's ETag
must_fix.evidence: send() hashes the buffered body (middleware/etag.go:130-133). Probe wrapping http.ServeContent(w, r, "a.txt", time.Unix(0,0), strings.NewReader("hello world")) in middleware.ETag printed: `GET 200 etag="b94d27b9…cde9" cl=11` vs `HEAD 200 etag="e3b0c442…b855" cl=11` (sha256 of the empty string). RFC 9110 §9.3.2 says HEAD should send the same header fields as GET. TestETagHEAD (etag_test.go:141) only uses a handler that writes the body on HEAD, so it misses this.

report:
I'd hold the merge for one bug. Otherwise the change is clean: `go vet ./...`, `go test ./...` and `make test`-style `go test -race -v ./middleware` all pass (20 ETag tests), and `gofmt -l .` prints nothing. The README row and its link are both there, and the tests sit next to the middleware.

**Must fix: a HEAD request gets a different ETag than GET when the handler doesn't write a body for HEAD.** For HEAD, `send` (`middleware/etag.go:130-133`) hashes whatever the handler buffered. Handlers that follow the standard library's own convention write nothing for HEAD; `http.ServeContent` and `http.FileServer` both skip the body copy when the method is HEAD. So HEAD gets the SHA-256 of an empty body, which isn't the tag GET returns for the same resource. RFC 9110 §9.3.2 says HEAD should send the same header fields as GET. A client that checks or caches a validator with HEAD will get a tag that never matches. I reproduced it with a temporary probe package under `middleware/` (deleted afterwards), wrapping `http.ServeContent(w, r, "a.txt", time.Unix(0,0), strings.NewReader("hello world"))` in `middleware.ETag`:

```
GET  200 etag="b94d27b9934d3e08a52e52d7da7dabfac484efe37a5380ee9088f7ace2efcde9" cl=11
HEAD 200 etag="e3b0c44298fc1c149afbf4c8996fb92427ae41e4649b934ca495991b7852b855" cl=11
```

`e3b0c442…` is the SHA-256 of an empty string, even though `Content-Length` is 11. `TestETagHEAD` (`middleware/etag_test.go:141`) misses this because its handler writes the body on HEAD too. One fix is to not generate a tag for HEAD when the buffered body is empty but the handler declared a non-zero `Content-Length`. The other is to document the limitation. Either way it needs a test with a handler that skips the body on HEAD.

Everything else I tried behaved correctly:
- **`If-None-Match` parsing:** weak/strong comparison, multiple header lines, commas inside quotes, malformed members and `*` only on a 200 response.
- **Response handling:** 1xx statuses and header snapshots behave like `net/http`, and so do hijack, push, unwrap and trailers.

There are no unrelated edits or leftover files. `CHANGELOG.md` stopped being kept up after v5.0.12, so not adding an entry isn't a convention miss. `git status` is the same as when I started.
